title: Lines, Angles, and Triangle Properties
concept: Most angle questions are solved with four facts and one warning. The facts: angles on a straight line add to 180° (supplementary); vertical angles — the pair across an X-shaped intersection — are equal; the three interior angles of a triangle add to 180°; and an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles (not all three). When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles and alternate interior angles are EQUAL, while co-interior (same-side interior) angles are SUPPLEMENTARY — they add to 180°. The warning: only use a relationship the problem actually gives you. On the SAT you may not assume two angles are equal just because the picture looks that way; the lines must be marked parallel or the angles marked equal. Set the correct relationship equal (or summing to 180°), then solve — usually a single clean linear step.

workedExamples.problem: Lines l and m are parallel, cut by a transversal. One angle measures 110°. What is the measure of its co-interior (same-side interior) angle?
steps: Co-interior angles between parallel lines are supplementary: they add to 180°.
Check: alternate interior angles would instead be equal (110°) — pick the right pair.

workedExamples.problem: A triangular truss has interior angles of 47° and 63°. What is the third angle?
steps: The three interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°.

trapPatterns: assumed_equal_without_label: treating two angles as equal because they look equal, when the figure never marks the lines parallel or the angles congruent.
confused_supplementary_complementary: using 180° when the angles are complementary (90°), or 90° when they are supplementary (180°).
exterior_angle_error: adding all three interior angles (or setting the exterior angle to one interior angle) instead of exterior = sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles.
parallel_line_confusion: mixing up alternate interior angles (equal) with co-interior angles (supplementary).
wrong_angle_pair: identifying the wrong pair — e.g. reading corresponding angles as supplementary, or vertical angles as supplementary.
calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically for every problem — angle chasing is a one- or two-step calculation by hand (set the correct relationship equal or summing to 180° and solve). Desmos adds nothing here.

problems.question: A straight road is crossed by a fence, forming two angles on one side of the road that together make a straight line. One of the angles measures 125°. What is the measure of the other angle?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: treated the two angles as vertical (equal) instead of a linear pair on a straight line.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: confused_supplementary_complementary: subtracted from 90° instead of 180°, treating the pair as complementary.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: added 125 to 180 instead of subtracting it from 180.

explanation: Angles that form a straight line are supplementary — they add to 180°.
So the other angle is 180° − 125°.
Compute: 55°.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — a linear pair sums to 180°, so the second angle is 180 − 125 = 55.

problems.question: A triangular roof truss has interior angles measuring 47° and 63°. What is the measure, in degrees, of the third interior angle?
explanation: The three interior angles of a triangle add to 180°.
So the third angle is 180° − 47° − 63°.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — triangle angles sum to 180°, so the third is 180 − 47 − 63 = 70.

problems.question: In the figure, lines l and m are parallel and are cut by a transversal. An angle at the upper intersection measures 72°. What is the measure of its corresponding angle at the lower intersection?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: parallel_line_confusion: treated corresponding angles as supplementary (like co-interior angles) instead of equal.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: confused_supplementary_complementary: subtracted from 90° as if the angles were complementary.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: halved the 72° instead of recognizing corresponding angles are congruent.

explanation: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, corresponding angles are equal.
So the corresponding angle equals the given 72°.
The measure is 72°.
Check: corresponding and alternate interior angles are equal; only co-interior angles would be supplementary (108°).
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — corresponding angles across parallel lines are congruent, so the angle is 72°.

problems.question: A road crosses two parallel streets, forming a transversal. At the first street the road makes a 65° angle. What is the measure of the co-interior (same-side interior) angle at the second street?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: parallel_line_confusion: treated co-interior angles as equal (like alternate interior angles) instead of supplementary.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: added 65 to 360 − ... reflex error, adding instead of subtracting from 180.

explanation: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles between parallel lines are supplementary — they add to 180°.
So the co-interior angle is 180° − 65°.
Compute: 115°.
Check: alternate interior angles would be 65° (equal); co-interior are supplementary (115°).
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — co-interior angles sum to 180°, so the angle is 180 − 65 = 115.

problems.question: In a triangle, the second angle is twice the first and the third angle is 30° larger than the first. Using that the three angles sum to 180°, what is the measure, in degrees, of the first angle?
explanation: Let x be the first angle. The angles are x, 2x, and x + 30.
Subtract 30: 4x = 150, so x = 37.5°.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — write x + 2x + (x + 30) = 180, combine to 4x + 30 = 180, and solve for x.

problems.question: Two fences cross, forming an X. One of the four angles at the crossing measures 40°. What is the measure of the angle directly across from it (its vertical angle)?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: used the adjacent (supplementary) angle, 180 − 40, instead of the vertical angle.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: confused_supplementary_complementary: subtracted from 90° as if the vertical angle were complementary.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: assumed_equal_without_label: halved the angle on a hunch instead of using that vertical angles are congruent.

explanation: Vertical angles — the pair directly across an X-shaped intersection — are always equal.
So the angle across from 40° also measures 40°.
The measure is 40°.
Check: the adjacent angles (140°) are supplementary, not the vertical one.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — vertical angles are congruent, so the opposite angle is 40°.

problems.question: A triangular bracket has two remote (non-adjacent) interior angles measuring 55° and 65°. At the third vertex, the side is extended to form an exterior angle. What is the measure of that exterior angle?

choices.label: B
choices.trap: exterior_angle_error: found the third interior angle (180 − 55 − 65 = 60), which is the angle adjacent to the exterior one, not the exterior angle itself.

choices.label: C
choices.trap: exterior_angle_error: added all three interior angles (55 + 65 + 60) instead of only the two non-adjacent ones.

choices.label: D
choices.trap: wrong_angle_pair: added just one remote interior angle to the adjacent interior angle (65 + 60) instead of the two remote angles.

explanation: The exterior angle theorem: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.
The remote interior angles are 55° and 65°.
So the exterior angle is 55 + 65 = 120°.
Check: the adjacent interior angle is 180 − 120 = 60°, matching 180 − 55 − 65.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — exterior angle = sum of the two remote interior angles = 55 + 65 = 120.

problems.question: In the figure, lines l and m are parallel and cut by a transversal. One interior angle on the same side as another is labeled (3x + 10)° and its co-interior angle is labeled (x + 50)°. Because these co-interior angles are supplementary, what is the value of x?
explanation: Co-interior (same-side interior) angles between parallel lines are supplementary, so they sum to 180°.
Write the equation: (3x + 10) + (x + 50) = 180.
Combine: 4x + 60 = 180, so 4x = 120.
Divide by 4: x = 30. Check: the angles are 100° and 80°, and 100 + 80 = 180.
problems.calculatorStrategy: solve_algebraically — co-interior angles are supplementary, so (3x + 10) + (x + 50) = 180; solve 4x + 60 = 180 for x.
